mainTopic: Rules learned from the way הלל was recited, and the principle of שומע כעונה
overview: Here, the גמרא lists important הלכות learned from the old way of saying הלל. A leader read הלל aloud, and the congregation answered in different ways at different points. Each pattern teaches a rule: answering הללויה, what to do when a גדול or a קטן reads for you, repeating the ראשי פרקים, doubling verses, and שומע כעונה. רבי חייא בר אבא is then asked whether someone who only heard, and said nothing, is יוצא. He answers that all the leading authorities say he is. בר קפרא proves שומע כעונה from יאשיהו, who is called the reader of words that שפן read to him. רב אחא בר יעקב defends that proof from the words 'when you heard'. Finally, רבא rules that 'ברוך הבא בשם ה׳' should be said together without a pause, and רב ספרא's response continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Many strong rules come from the custom of reciting הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that many important הלכות can be learned from how הלל was customarily recited.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are many important laws we can learn from the custom of how הלל was said.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us a list is coming: rules learned from the way people used to say הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In earlier times not everyone knew הלל by heart. A leader read it aloud and the congregation answered. The exact pattern of those answers became the source for several הלכות, which the גמרא now lists one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: הלל, the psalms of praise (תהלים 113 to 118)

phrases.english: There are strong (important) laws to learn
phrases.notes: This line is part of a statement of רבא that begins on the previous amud.

phrases.english: from the custom of Hallel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִלְכְתָא גִּיבָּרָתָא אִיכָּא לְמִשְׁמַע מִמִּנְהֲגָא דְהַלֵּילָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the list of rules derived from the הלל custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The custom of reciting הלל is a source for several important הלכות.

steps.title: Answering הללויה is a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The leader says הללויה and the congregation answers הללויה, which teaches that answering הללויה is a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leader says 'הללויה' and the people answer 'הללויה'. From here we learn that it is a מצוה to answer 'הללויה'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first rule on the list: when the leader says הללויה, the people answer הללויה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the congregation answered with the word הללויה, the גמרא learns that this answer is a real מצוה and not just a habit.

phrases.english: He (the leader) says: 'Halleluya',
and they (the congregation) say: 'Halleluya'
From here we learn that it is a מצוה to answer 'Halleluya'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first item in the list announced in step 1.

steps.title: When an adult reads הלל for you, answer הללויה
steps.stepSummary: The leader says 'הללו עבדי ה׳' and the people answer only הללויה, which is the source for the משנה's rule about a גדול reading for someone.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leader says 'הללו עבדי ה׳' and the people answer 'הללויה'. From here we learn that if an adult reads הלל for someone, that person answers 'הללויה' after him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second rule: the people do not repeat the leader's words. They just answer הללויה. That teaches what to do when a גדול reads הלל for you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The congregation did not repeat 'הללו עבדי ה׳'. They only said הללויה as a response. This shows that when a גדול, who is himself obligated, reads for you, his reading counts for you, so you only need to answer הללויה and not repeat everything.

keyTerms.meaning: An adult, who is obligated in the מצוה
Reads it out for him, leads him in it

phrases.english: He says: 'Praise, servants of the Lord',
and they say: 'Halleluya'

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן שֶׁאִם הָיָה גָּדוֹל מַקְרֶא אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: From here we learn that if an adult was reading it for him,
he answers 'Halleluya' after him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״הַלָּלוּ עַבְדֵי ה׳״, וְהֵן אוֹמְרִין: ״הַלְלוּיָהּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the list, giving a source for the earlier משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a גדול reads הלל for someone, that person answers only הללויה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a source for the rule in the משנה about who can read הלל for others.

steps.title: Repeating the opening verses of sections
steps.stepSummary: The leader says 'הודו לה׳' and the people repeat 'הודו לה׳', which teaches that it is a מצוה to answer with the ראשי פרקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leader says 'הודו לה׳' and the people say 'הודו לה׳'. From here we learn that it is a מצוה to answer with the opening lines of the sections.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third rule: at 'הודו לה׳' the people repeat the leader's exact words, because it is the opening verse of a section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to here the congregation only answered הללויה. Here they repeat the line itself. This teaches that opening verses (ראשי פרקים) such as 'הודו לה׳ כי טוב' are repeated by the listeners as a refrain.

phrases.english: He says: 'Give thanks to the Lord',
and they say: 'Give thanks to the Lord'
From here we learn that it is a מצוה to answer with the beginnings of sections.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״הוֹדוּ לַה׳״, וְהֵן אוֹמְרִים: ״הוֹדוּ לַה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the list. This time the people repeat the leader's words instead of answering הללויה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is a מצוה to repeat the ראשי פרקים.

steps.title: רב חנן בר רבא says the same rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support: רב חנן בר רבא also taught that it is a מצוה to answer ראשי פרקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught that רב חנן בר רבא said: it is a מצוה to answer with the opening lines of the sections.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the previous rule by quoting an אמורא who said exactly the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'איתמר נמי' means the rule just learned from the custom was also stated directly as a הלכה. This shows the rule does not rest only on how people used to behave.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (a support from another teaching)
An אמורא who taught this rule

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא:
phrases.english: It was also stated: Rav Chanan bar Rava said:
It is a מצוה to answer with the beginnings of sections.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 4 with a matching statement from an אמורא.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one must answer ראשי פרקים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A direct teaching of רב חנן בר רבא

steps.title: When a child reads הלל for you, repeat every word
steps.stepSummary: The leader says 'אנא ה׳ הושיעה נא' and the people repeat it word for word, which teaches that when a קטן reads for you, you repeat everything he says.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leader says 'אנא ה׳ הושיעה נא' and the people say 'אנא ה׳ הושיעה נא'. From here we learn that if a child reads it for someone, he repeats after him whatever he says.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth rule: the people repeat a line that is not an opening verse. That teaches what to do when a קטן reads הלל for you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אנא ה׳ הושיעה נא' is not a ראש פרק, yet the people still repeat it fully. A קטן is not obligated, so his reading cannot count for you, and you must say every word yourself. This is unlike the case of the גדול in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, who is not obligated in the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 3. With a גדול you only answer הללויה. With a קטן you repeat every word, because his reading does not count for you.

phrases.english: He says: 'Please, Lord, save us',
and they say: 'Please, Lord, save us'

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן שֶׁאִם הָיָה קָטָן מַקְרֶא אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: From here we learn that if a minor was reading it for him,
one repeats after him whatever he says.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״אָנָא ה׳ הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא״, וְהֵן אוֹמְרִים: ״אָנָּא ה׳ הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list and sets up a contrast with the גדול case in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a קטן reads הלל for someone, that person repeats every word.

steps.title: Repeating a verse twice is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The leader says 'אנא ה׳ הצליחה נא' and the people repeat it, which teaches that one may repeat verses (כפילה) in הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leader says 'אנא ה׳ הצליחה נא' and the people say 'אנא ה׳ הצליחה נא'. From here we learn that if someone wants to say a verse twice, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fifth rule: from this repeated line we learn that saying a verse twice in הלל is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition here shows that doubling verses is a proper part of הלל and not an improper addition. This matches the משנה's rule that where the custom is to repeat, one repeats.

phrases.english: He says: 'Please, Lord, grant us success'
and they say: 'Please, Lord, grant us success'
From here we learn that if one wishes to repeat, he may repeat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״אָנָא ה׳ הַצְלִיחָה נָּא״ וְהֵן אוֹמְרִים: ״אָנָּא ה׳ הַצְלִיחָה נָּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next item in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may repeat verses in הלל.

steps.title: One who hears is like one who says
steps.stepSummary: The leader says 'ברוך הבא' and the people finish with 'בשם ה׳', which teaches שומע כעונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leader says 'ברוך הבא' and the people say 'בשם ה׳'. From here we learn that one who hears is like one who answers.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last rule on the list: the people never said the first half of the verse, yet they are counted as having said it, because they heard it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The congregation only said the second half of the verse. For them to have fulfilled the whole verse, hearing the first half from the leader must count as saying it. This is the source for שומע כעונה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In the name of the Lord', the end of that verse
One who hears is like one who says it himself

steps.whatToRemember: The way people answered in הלל teaches six things: answering הללויה is a מצוה; with a גדול reading for you, answer הללויה; repeat ראשי פרקים; with a קטן reading for you, repeat everything; repeating verses is allowed; and שומע כעונה.
steps.whyThisMatters: שומע כעונה is a basic rule used across many מצוות, such as hearing קידוש or מגילה from someone else.

phrases.english: He says: 'Blessed is the one who comes',
and they say: 'in the name of the Lord'
From here we learn that one who hears is like one who answers.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״בָּרוּךְ הַבָּא״, וְהֵן אוֹמְרִים: ״בְּשֵׁם ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final item in the list of rules from the הלל custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שומע כעונה: hearing counts as saying.

steps.title: Is one who only heard, but did not answer, יוצא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא is asked whether a person who heard the recitation but did not say it himself has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי חייא בר אבא: If someone heard but did not answer, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא is asked a straightforward question: is listening alone enough? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 showed the people saying only 'בשם ה׳'. That means they at least said something. This question goes further and asks about a person who said nothing at all and only listened.

keyTerms.meaning: He heard but did not answer

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: They asked Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
If one heard and did not answer, what is the law?
phrases.notes: This means hearing the recitation without repeating it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 8's idea of שומע כעונה to someone who answers nothing at all.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a listener who did not recite anything has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.title: All the leading teachers said: he is יוצא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא answers that the Sages, teachers, leaders and expounders all held that one who heard without answering is יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The Sages, the teachers, the heads of the nation and the expounders all said: one who heard and did not answer has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers the question. Hearing alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not give a reason here. Instead he cites a broad consensus of every type of authority. This shows the rule was widely accepted. The next step supplies a source from a פסוק.

phrases.english: He said to them: the Sages and the teachers
and the heads of the nation and the expounders said:
One who heard and did not answer has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A listener is יוצא even without answering, according to all the leading authorities.

steps.title: A פסוק source: יאשיהו is called the reader, though שפן read
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא proves שומע כעונה from a פסוק that credits יאשיהו with reading the ספר, even though another פסוק says שפן read it to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי שמעון בן פזי said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי, quoting בר קפרא: From where do we know that hearing is like answering? Because it is written, 'the words which יאשיהו read.' But did יאשיהו read them? Didn't שפן read them, as it is written, 'and שפן read it before the king'? Rather, from here we learn that one who hears is like one who answers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the ruling of step 10 from a פסוק. One פסוק says יאשיהו read, and another says שפן read. The two fit together only if hearing counts as reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by pointing out a contradiction between two פסוקים. יאשיהו only listened while שפן read aloud. Yet the פסוק says יאשיהו 'read'. So the פסוק treats the listener as if he were the reader.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (a supporting teaching)
One who hears is like one who answers

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source for שומע כעונה. That principle is behind hearing קידוש, מגילה and שופר from someone else.

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
phrases.english: It was also stated: Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם בַּר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in the name of Bar Kappara:
From where do we know that one who hears is like one who answers?
As it is written: 'the words which Josiah read.'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from מלכים ב 22:16.

phrases.english: But did Josiah read them?
Didn't Shaphan read them?

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיִּקְרָאֵהוּ שָׁפָן (אֵת כׇּל הַדְּבָרִים הָאֵלֶּה) לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ״.
phrases.english: As it is written: 'And Shaphan read it before the king.'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from מלכים ב 22:10.

phrases.english: Rather, from here we learn that one who hears is like one who answers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a פסוק-based source for the ruling of step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who hears without answering is יוצא (שומע כעונה).
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים ב 22:16 credits יאשיהו with reading, while 22:10 says שפן read to him.

steps.title: Maybe יאשיהו read it himself afterward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: perhaps after שפן read, יאשיהו read it again on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps after שפן read them, יאשיהו read them himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in the proof from step 11. Maybe both men really read it, one after the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יאשיהו also read it himself, the פסוק that calls him the reader is simply literal. Then there is no proof that hearing counts as reading.

phrases.english: But perhaps after Shaphan read them
Josiah read them himself?

steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of שומע כעונה from the יאשיהו פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both פסוקים can be literally true if each man read at a different time. That leaves nothing to learn.

steps.title: The פסוק says 'when you heard,' not 'when you read'
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב defends the proof. The prophecy praises יאשיהו for humbling himself when he heard, which shows that his hearing was what counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Don't think that. For it is written: 'Because your heart was tender and you humbled yourself before ה׳ when you heard these words.' It says 'when you heard,' not 'when you read.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב rejects the idea that יאשיהו read it again later. He shows from the פסוק that יאשיהו reacted right away, upon hearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ties יאשיהו's response to his hearing. That means he did not read it again before reacting. So the earlier פסוק that calls him the 'reader' must be counting his hearing as reading, and the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not enter your mind (that idea is impossible)

steps.whatToRemember: שומע כעונה: someone who listens with intent is treated as if he said the words himself. The source is יאשיהו, who is called the 'reader' of what שפן read to him.

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
Don't even think that,
for it is written: 'Because your heart was tender
and you humbled yourself before the Lord
when you heard these words'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is from מלכים ב 22:19.

phrases.english: 'When you heard', and not 'when you read.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12 and restores the proof of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual precision: the wording of a third פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יאשיהו might have read the text himself after שפן did.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק links his humility to hearing, so his hearing is what counted as 'reading'. שומע כעונה is proven.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One who hears is like one who answers.

steps.title: Say ברוך הבא בשם ה׳ together, without a break
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that one should not pause between 'ברוך הבא' and 'בשם ה׳', but should say the phrase as one unit. רב ספרא then begins to respond.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A person should not say 'ברוך הבא' and then afterward 'בשם ה׳'. Rather he should say 'ברוך הבא בשם ה׳' together. רב ספרא said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the practical words of הלל. רבא gives a rule about how to say this פסוק. The last line sets up רב ספרא's response, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 8, the leader said 'ברוך הבא' and the people finished with 'בשם ה׳'. רבא now teaches that a person should not pause between 'ברוך הבא' and 'בשם ה׳'. The phrase should be said as one connected unit.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא's rule is about not pausing in the middle of this פסוק. It does not take back the שומע כעונה lesson that step 8 learned from the people finishing the פסוק. רב ספרא's reaction comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A person should not say 'Blessed is the one who comes'
and then afterward 'in the name of the Lord',
rather, 'Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord', together.
Rav Safra said to him:
phrases.notes: רב ספרא's answer starts here and carries on to the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the שומע כעונה discussion back to the wording of הלל, specifically the פסוק from step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברוך הבא בשם ה׳ should be recited as one continuous phrase, not split with a pause.
